$comment: Sizes are world pixels (320 x 180 view). This level is not painted: everything in it is flat, unlit pixel art drawn in code at 1 world px, black-figure on clay, exempt from the painted style of content/README.md (LEVEL.md, Art, ruled 2026-10-10). No entry has a file and none is wanted; each note is what the code must draw, written before it is drawn. dx and dy place a sprite from the box its entity moves: Theseus's 12 x 24, the bull's head's 11 x 10. Not listed: the holes, which are only the masonry's absence; the hatch, a plain hole like every other; the HUD and the map pin, which stay as they are (2026-10-10). The tourist's own frames, his deaths among them, are the chapter's, in ../shared.

assets.what: The clay: the air of the whole level, outside the door and inside the labyrinth, one flat colour to the edges of the screen. No sky.
The heavier glaze ground line the queue, Ariadne and the kneeling hero stand on, 2 px between two reserved lines: the panel's lower border.

A band of black rays rising from below, as at an amphora's foot, in the strip of ground outside the door under the ground line: ten tall glaze triangles, points up, standing on the course line with clay between them. Never spikes, a hazard or a platform.

The labyrinth's outer face: a glaze contour down the wall over the door, along the top of the roof and down beside the rays under the ground line, and the door's lintel, so that outside and inside are told apart by the wall alone.
The post in the door's thickness that Theseus ties the thread to.
The black vestibule behind the door, in full glaze: the dark the hero walks into and the body is dragged out of.

The labyrinth's masonry, by rule: a dilute-glaze wash in square blocks two tiles each way, a full-glaze line at each course's foot and under any block over air, and a joint only where two stones meet. Every solid tile in the level but the lip.
The same masonry with air over it: identical to tile-labyrinth, with no lit top.
One of the six youths of the tribute, waiting in the file at the door, a figure every 6 px: all glaze, beardless, a red fillet, empty hands, no incision down his body. Faces right.
One of the seven maidens of the tribute, waiting in the file at the door, a figure every 6 px: a peplos in glaze, her face, arm and feet in cream. Faces right.
Ariadne, apart from the file, facing the door from the first frame to the last: a maiden with added red on her fillet and her hem, her near hand open and empty. Faces right.
Theseus on one knee at the doorpost, tying the thread: wrap over, wrap under, tug, pick. The figure every other Theseus pose is drawn from. Faces right.

A 1 px line of reserved clay round the tourist's top and sides, corners included, and under him only while he is off his feet, drawn only where glaze is behind him, so that the one full-colour figure is cut from the black as the vase painters cut one figure from the next.

Ariadne's thread, the one pure white in the level, in all its states: the knot on the post, the slack on the passage floor, the line rising and taut at y 149, let go, laid down the hero's route, the loops he paid out, the ball in his hand.
The ball of thread at the line's inner end, on the passage floor under O1, and later in the hero's doorway. Plain white.
The knob on the passage's back wall that the hero's trailing foot pushes off as he mantles up O1: a small glaze silhouette on the clay, round and filled, never a ring. Background, never rock.
Theseus up from the knee and leaning back on the line to test his knot, both hands on it at the post: upright, half, and full, 6 px back at the head and his front leg braced. Faces right.
Theseus standing: a beardless youth in a short chiton, the sword at his hip in its scabbard; and at guard in the fight, the sword drawn and upright in his right fist. Faces right.

Theseus walking and running: two strides looking ahead, the same two with his head turned back over his shoulder at his knot, and the same two at guard as he steps out of his doorway into the fight. Faces right.
Theseus mantling 80 px up O1, both arms up in front of his face to the lip: with both legs under him, and with the near leg only, while the code draws the trailing one out to the boss. Faces right.

Theseus dropping straight down a shaft, feet first, his front arm up before his face with the ball, his back arm flung out behind him and down, never two uprights either side of his head; never jumping. Faces right.
Theseus crouched on his heels where he landed, paying out a loop of thread: the arm at four quarters of its circle while the white loop grows. Faces right.

The beast's breath: twin plumes of dust out of the hatch, or through the bed block's joint, rising 32 px and drawn back in; the puffs of its clock; the sniff, the jet and the settling of the snort. Grains, never a line or a solid.
The lip, buried: the dressed threshold with stone over it. The game asks for this id but never draws it here, since the lip always has air over it.
The lip: the one dressed stone in the floor, before the hatch, its top dished by two worn foot hollows where the tribute stood. Edged in glaze, so it reads as stone.
The black doorway on row 5 where Theseus waits unseen for the fight, framed in a glaze line on the back wall. Background, never a ledge.

The Minotaur's man's body, drawn by code in flat glaze: the back on its solid every frame, the neck, arms pixelled as the people are, the upper arm thicker than the forearm, bent at the elbow and narrowed to a wrist, the folded leg a filled wedge, never a letter or a digit; crouched, gripped, on its knee, heaving, lurching on both knees, tossing, its head swung back under a man on its back, kneeling up before the second blow. Theseus stands between its body and its near arm. Size as crouched, with its stones.

The bull's head on the man's body, horns and all, a lyre of 2 px horns: level, tossed up, and down on the floor lying on its cheek, its horns up at its back. Faces right; the game flips it to face left.

The Minotaur's hand, a man's, oversized: flat on a stone, gripping it, its palm on the top, its fingers down the stone's face and its thumb laid forward along the stone's top on the palm's last row, parted by the one incision; holding the stone up on its fist, two fingertips on its face; clawing, raised, three fingers hooked forward at its top and the thumb out forward under them; upright and edge-on as a palm for the clap; and reaching, the same hand closed, its fingers together and the thumb out under them. Never a hoof, never a rake. Up to 8 x 12 a frame. Faces right; the game flips it to face left.
One of the Minotaur's two stones, in cream outlined in glaze: a hand flat on each, the near one raised at the grip, swung at the hero and set down. Never thrown.

The Minotaur after the second blow: the body sunk over its knees and bowed, its back on the 24 px solid, its neck bowed down to its head on the floor before it, clear of Theseus's feet; nothing incised across it. Bloodless. It stays. Drawn by code, facing left.
Theseus leaping low over the crouched bull onto its horn, the vases' warrior with his sword up over his head and back, his far arm out ahead, never a bull-leaper. Faces right.

Theseus braced at the bull's head, the horn in his left hand while it is in his reach (drawn by code), the sword held up in his right; and shoved, leaning into it as the struck body's lurch carries him. Faces right.
Theseus down under the stone the bull heaves at him, his head under its arc, his hand let go of the horn, the sword low. Faces right.
Theseus with the sword drawn back over his shoulder, against the clay, before each blow. Faces right.
Theseus lunging in past the bull's near arm, the sword struck home: the first blow under its jaw into its throat, and the second rising into the throat of its jerked-up head. Faces right.
Theseus in the closing tableau, leaning into the pull, the dead Minotaur's horn in his far hand behind him: two strides. Faces right; the game flips it to face left, the way he walks.

The dead Minotaur in the closing tableau, on its front, dragged by a horn, a man's silhouette in its outline: its head down across the threshold, a shoulder, an arm trailing, a knee bent with the shin up, the rest in the vestibule in a reserved outline. Drawn by code, facing left.
